metadata.summary: Jacob Fearnley retired with an injury after losing 5-1 in the first set against Arthur Fery to give his fellow countryman a place in the second round at the Vienna Open.

Fearnley was broken by Fery in just his second service game, with the British No 1 winning the next two games on the bounce and looking set to consign his opponent to a comprehensive first-set loss. Fearnley, though, then put a stop to the contest, shaking the umpire's hand and retiring with an unspecified injury, allowing Fery safe passage to the next stage of the competition. metadata.content: Alexia Putellas wins Ballon d'Or: How the Women's Super League has benefitted from the midfielder's immense influence | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Breaking Alexia Putellas wins Ballon d'Or: How the Women's Super League has benefitted from the midfielder's immense influence London City Lionesses star Alexia Putellas wins 2026 Women's Ballon d'Or for record-equalling third time; Putellas captained Barcelona to quadruple last season; watch London City Lionesses vs Man City Women on Saturday, live on Sky Sports Premier League, kick-off 12pm Laura Hunter Football Features Writer Monday 26 October 2026 22:55, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Alexia Putellas makes WSL history after winning Ballon d'Or. London City Lionesses star Alexia Putellas claimed a record-equalling third women's Ballon d'Or. The Spain international captained Barcelona to a quadruple last season, including Champions League glory, as she scored 26 goals and provided 15 assists for club and country. The 32-year-old then sensationally joined London City Lionesses in one of the biggest transfers in WSL history. Since her move in July, Putellas has scored three goals and has an assist in her seven WSL games. More to follow... metadata.content: Ballon d'Or 2026: Harry Kane, Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal in race for men's award - stats and pundits' opinions | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Analysis Ballon d'Or 2026: Harry Kane, Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal in race for men's award - stats and pundits' opinions Harry Kane, Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe battling for 2026 men's Ballon d'Or on Monday; Kane odds-on favourite to become first Englishman to win the award in 25 years; Lamine Yamal, 19, aiming to become youngest-ever Ballon d'Or winner; Sky Sports' Jamie Carragher backing Kane to win By Declan Olley & Adam Smith Monday 26 October 2026 22:52, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Take a look at who Sky Sports pundits and journalists are backing to win the 2026 Ballon d'Or Harry Kane is the odds-on favourite to win the 2026 men’s Ballon d’Or, which could be one of the tightest results in recent history. England captain and Bayern Munich striker Kane is the bookmakers' favourite to become the first Englishman to win the award since Michael Owen in 2001. Victory would see Kane become just the fifth English winner of the Ballon d'Or after Sir Stanley Matthews, Sir Bobby Charlton, Kevin Keegan and Owen, while he would also become the first Bayern player to claim it in 45 years.
